classification.difficultyReason: Translate each story into an ordered sequence of speed changes and match that sequence to a graph. Distinguishing steady motion, acceleration, continued full speed and rapid versus gradual stopping requires routine linked interpretation across words and graphs.

content.prompt: Match the graph with one of the stories.

spec.description: Three positive horizontal plateaus with short smooth rises between them; arrowed axes and an unnumbered rectangular grid.
spec.mathematics: Three successive constant speeds, each greater than the previous speed. Coordinates are schematic drawing coordinates; no numerical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no matching answer is printed.

spec.description: Long low positive plateau, increasingly steep rise to a short high plateau, then a steep fall curving towards zero.
spec.mathematics: Initially constant positive speed, followed by increasing speed and rapid stopping. No numerical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no matching answer is printed.

spec.description: Curve rises from the axes' intersection with increasing steepness, then joins a long horizontal plateau.
spec.mathematics: Speed increases from zero, then remains constant at a positive value. No numerical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no matching answer is printed.

spec.description: Increasingly steep rise from zero, rounded broad maximum, then a descending segment ending at zero speed.
spec.mathematics: Speed increases to a maximum, then gradually decreases to zero. No numerical scale is supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent supplied graph; no matching answer is printed.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Jenny climbs a hill at a steady speed and then runs down the hill stopping as quickly as possible.

answer.worked: B. The initial horizontal segment shows steady speed. The speed then increases before dropping rapidly to zero.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Peter starts slowly and increases his speed until he is running as fast as possible then gradually slows.

answer.worked: D. The speed increases from zero to a maximum, then gradually decreases to zero.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Danielle gradually increases her speed and when at full speed continues to run.

answer.worked: C. The rising curve shows increasing speed. The horizontal segment shows that she continues at constant speed.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Brook walks for a while then jogs for a while then runs for a while.

answer.worked: A. The three horizontal segments show three constant speeds, increasing from walking to jogging to running.
